t: You're in St James's Park, a twenty-three hectare Royal Park in the City of Westminster. The area was first enclosed as a deer park near the Palace of Whitehall for Henry the Eighth in the 1530s. It's the most easterly of a chain of parks that includes Green Park, Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens. Several people have links to it. Charlotte Lee, Lady Baltimore, a granddaughter of Charles the Second, was born here, as was the cricketer Harry Cornish. George Burrington, a governor of North Carolina, died here.
